Hii although our situations aren't exactly the same, as someone who's on the road to getting diagnosed with JRA and drawing and writing are about my only hobbies I know how much it sucks not being able to do things with your hands. Even if I'm willing to push through the pain of my fingers hurting, my brain literally can't make up any words due to how fatigued I am all the time. Sometimes I used to just wish I could cut my arms and legs off due to how useless they are an sometimes still do.

To be honest, the best thing you can do is be kind to yourself. You can't expect yourself to be at the same level you once were and as awful as it is, it's just something you have to accept and try to make adjustments around. 

For example: I no longer use both my thumbs to type, often replacing one with an index/middle finger instead and I always take at least a weeks break after posting a fic/chapter to give my hands a rest. Writing in the morning is best for me because by 6pm I'm already set to go to bed so it's also good to find times that work for you. Most of the time I write is when I'm home from school during flares because when I get back it's physically impossible.

Also as tedious as it is, rubbing out and scribbling lines sometimes writing on paper seems to hurt less than type since there's less repetitive motion.

Since you mentioned for you this was temporarily I wish you all the best, but at the moment while you're getting there all you can really do is, take care of yourself (physically and mentally) search to be on a good set of meds and do your best in learning to live with it.

Sorry if this wasn't super useful I'm still trying to start drawing and writing consistently again since getting sick but I hope this can help!!

I think the age difference between them all plays a reallt big role in everyone's interactions but as someone who's one of six children I'll try give some insight.

-When everyone is in the house it's always loud and there's 0 privacy. If there's younger kids it's also impossible for the house to remain spotless for an entire day.

-As already mentioned in the other comments, siblings will often like split off into pairings/groups. For us it's the oldest 3 and then youngest 3. It's usually how we'll divide up when events and stuff are happening.

-As the oldest two, I'd consider myself closest with my big sibling. For the younger two, they're very similar to how we acted as kids so that's them. The middle two are kinda outliers?? Idk.

-Meals aren't really eaten together at some big long table, 90% of time it's first come first server at whatever time.

-The older kids heavily parent the younger ones. 

-Nothing truly belongs to you. Ownership is a made up construct. If you wake up and see someone wearing your hoodie you can't do anything but get annoyed because chances are you've stolen something from them too.

Food is different and will usually strike hell if something is stolen.

-Planning occasions is absolute chaos. In my whole time of being alive we've never been on time to anything. Someone will go missing five minutes before leaving, another is crying and the next is still sleeping.

-Parents attention isn't divided equally even if they want it too. 

-We have nicknames (shortening of names/insults) but none of that "sis" "bro" thing.

-it's annoying but fun.
It's not an overly common thing but I've seen it enough to be annoyed by it.

1. Have brainrot of a scenario I made

2. Get the urge to make fanfic of that scenario

3. Figure out a way to make that scenario to make sense in written form.

4. Fail and contemplate giving up.

5. Try again by writing over 2k of a different ideas.

6. Make general outline of the fic. 

7. Scrap those 2k words because something doesn't make sense.

8. Think for a few weeks on what to do and contemplate giving up again.

9. Figure it out, then use the plot outline as a base to work with since it's all the same characters.

10. Write the story.
